params.body:
#666 set this line back to serial because the step had gone from 225s to 264s. That was wrong, and
the reason is worth writing down: 225s was the fastest of a very noisy set, and I compared against
it as if it were the baseline.

The eight runs of this suite in this repository, oldest first:

| | |
|---|---|
| serial | 353s, 369s, 225s, 284s, 323s |
| parallel | 264s, 264s |

A single serial run says anything between 225s and 369s. Both parallel runs landed on 264s, and
that is the finding: two saturated processes are less at the mercy of whoever else is on the host
than one process waiting on it. That steadiness is worth more here than the factor of two that two
cores could never give anyway.

So `--parallel` comes back, and the comment above the line carries the table, so that the next
person reads the spread instead of one run. Everything the flag needs was already merged in #665
and stays as it is; the demo seeder trim from #666 stays too.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: Back to parallel in the CI: one run is not a measurement
